propositions: The divergent_implementation axis is miscalibrated: it fires on only 7.72% of plan-v3 findings despite governing the class of omitted-scope sites that represents ~90% of the 1,307 unenumerated-consumer findings, and it is the only hard-override axis never graded via worked examples or closed literal set.

The axis must be graded by divergence kind (contradicts_reality, omits_required_site, incomplete_enumeration, none) with floors at 0.85 for the first two and a soft contribution below 0.60 for the third, requiring refactoring impact_plan to exclude the axis from _SEV01 and drive it through a new DIVERGENCE_GRADE01 map.

A grade-set change to the verifier prompt must be paired with a rejection of purpose-built LLM eval suites as calibration instruments (ADR-0054), constraining future A/B testing to corpus replay and dogfooding rather than bulk re-review runs on cost grounds.

Applying a prod_impact floor (Fix 2) as an alternative to semantic grading (Fix 1) collides with the novelty convergence floor (0.4) and violates the loop-termination constraint, because prod_impact describes consequences rather than plan text and cannot be remediated by the author.

All existing fixtures grading divergent_implementation on the retired ordinal ladder must migrate to the closed Literal set, including an out-of-scope fixture at tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py:1282 that would break CI.

The corpus replay bounds (best: 249 block / worst: 686 block from 1,396 non-none findings) show a worst-case increase of 81 new blocks well below the 113-finding over-fire that a blunt widening would produce, and the realized distribution must be monitored during dogfooding to detect verifier bias toward cosmetic grades.
